pageCache.pageTitle: Chewton Mendip Church of England Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law. The teaching of British Values links closely with our school vision and aims where all are "Growing together."
The DfE have reinforced the need ‘to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of Law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.’
Democracy is when a group of people have equal rights and the freedom to choose how they are treated, rather than when one person has all the power and makes all the decisions. It can also refer to the way in which we vote for the person or group we want to represent us. Children are taught about democracy through our curriculum. We have a pupil voice (school council) who are elected by the other children in their class. Democracy is discussed during this process. Throughout our curriculum and in the day to day activities, children are given the opportunity to vote on different topics.
Individual liberty is when people have the freedom to choose their faith, beliefs, likes and dislikes which are outside Government control. We teach children that they are individuals and they are able to make decisions that may be different to their friends. These discussions happen during assemblies, PSHE and other lessons.
Rule of Law means that all people and groups are ruled by the same laws which help to keep us all safe and happy. We involve our children in setting rules for their class and the school. Where appropriate, children contribute to writing policies such as the behaviour policy. We discuss these as a whole school, in classes and on an individual basis.
Mutual respect is showing respect and tolerance towards people whose beliefs, traditions, race, culture and opinions may be different to our own, which is then shown back to us. Finding out about each other will help us to understand and to treat others in the way we would wish to be treated. Children are taught about mutual respect through assemblies and our curriculum.
Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs
Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs is showing respect towards people who share different beliefs and traditions to our own. We teach children how to respect each other and other members of our community through assemblies, PSHE lessons and across our curriculum.
We make links between our school values and British values and incorporate them into all that we do. They are woven throughout our curriculum and are demonstrated by all members of our community.

Vision and Aims
“The seed fell into good ground and grew up increasing and yielding thirty, sixty and a hundred times as much” Mark 4:8
We are “Growing Together” to become the best we can be and enjoy “life in all its fullness.” (John 10:10)
We are like the seeds growing in the good soil in the Parable of the Sower. We grow and learn together every day. Our school is the good soil where we are cared for, encouraged and helped to flourish.
Our values of Kindness, Respect, Perseverance, Responsibility, Honesty and Courage are the strong roots and enable us to try our best and become confident, caring people, following the teachings of Jesus.
Staff, pupils, families and the local community work together as a team to provide a safe, nurturing and inclusive environment for everyone to reach their full potential and achieve our school aims.
Our schools’ values combine the Church of England’s vision for education with our aims, and links closely with the PSHE curriculum.
The Church of England vision for education promotes:
Our values have been chosen to link with our curriculum and to support children to thrive and contribute to their communities, living well and growing together.
Each term we focus on one of our values. Our collective and class worship teaches children about the meaning of the value and links this with teachings from the Bible and with the themes in the Kapow PSHE curriculum. Our values are also carefully linked with the fundamental British values.
Our core values are:
Term 3: Perseverance
Term 4: Responsibility
Each week we lead a whole school collective worship introducing and discussing our values for the term, exploring related teachings from the Bible. In class worship children are able to further respond and reflect on the significance of these teachings in their own life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chewton Mendip Church of England Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Headteacher's Welcome
Thank you for taking the time to visit our school website.I am sure you will find an abundance of information about our school.
It is a privilege to lead a community where our Christian vision, “Growing Together to live life in all its fullness,” shapes everything we do. Our vision is rooted in Jesus’ Parable of the Sower, where the seed that falls into good soil “grew up, increasing and yielding thirty, sixty and a hundred times as much” (Mark 4:8). We believe our school is that good soil: a place where every child is nurtured, encouraged and supported to flourish.
Our Christian character is lived out daily through our values of Kindness, Respect, Perseverance, Responsibility, Honesty and Courage. These values act as strong roots that help our children grow into confident, compassionate and resilient individuals who follow the teachings of Jesus in how they learn, play and care for one another. They guide our relationships, shape our curriculum and inspire our pupils to make thoughtful, positive choices.
“Growing Together” is not just our motto; it is the way we live as a community. Staff, pupils, families, governors and the local parish work in partnership to create a safe, inclusive and nurturing environment where everyone is valued. Our Christian ethos strengthens this partnership, helping us build a school culture where children feel known, loved and able to achieve their full potential.
The impact of our Christian character reaches beyond the school gates. Our pupils learn to serve others, act responsibly and contribute to the wider community with kindness and courage. Through collective worship, community events, charitable work and strong links with the church, we encourage children to recognise their role in helping others flourish. In this way, our vision and aims make a real and lasting difference to the lives of families and the wider community we serve.
I warmly invite you to explore our website and discover more about how we grow, learn and flourish together. Thank you for visiting.
If you have any questions about our school or would like to visit please contact us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chewton Mendip Church of England Primary School - French
pageCache.text:
French
Mr. Newland teaches KS2 French with interactive lessons including songs and games to support their learning.
At the end of each year, Year 5 and 6 perform a well-known story to parents and the rest of our school entirely in French.
Optional Home learning:
To enrich the children's learning further, BBC Bitesize have games, skills lessons, crafts, songs and stories that can be accessed at: https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/subjects/z39d7ty Duolingo is a language app. You can learn vocabulary, conjugation, reading, writing, pronunciation, and listening skills on the app in a way that is competitive and fun.
Every Tuesday lunchtime, Mrs Pashley will be running a French Club for our Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 pupils.
This week, the children got off to a lovely start with a French song and met some rather cuddly characters to help them on their language-learning adventure! They also began learning how to introduce themselves in French.
Très bien, everyone! We look forward to seeing their French skills grow over the coming weeks! 🇫🇷
We were treated to the Year 6 French play yesterday afternoon—a wonderfully creative retelling of The Three Little Pigs in their own unique style! It was absolutely fantastic. The story was easy to follow, regardless of how much French we knew, and it was clear how much hard work had gone into the performance. A huge thank you to Year 6 and Mr Newland for all their efforts. We thoroughly enjoyed it, and the children’s French speaking was truly impressive. Bravo to everyone involved!

Maths
Alongside our maths curriculum, we are keen to offer opportunities that allow our pupils to develop a love of all areas of maths.
Wells Cathedral School Primary Maths Festival
On Wednesday 5th November, 4 members of Buzzard class had a fantastic time at a maths festival held at Wells Cathedral School! They designed a creative poster all about fractions, teamed up to tackle tricky problem-solving questions, and raced through a thrilling maths question relay.
Robin class designed number tracks to play race games with their Buzzard class buddies. Robin class had been playing a range of track games in the lead up to designing their own. They decided if they wanted a count down or race to a greater number before they added a decorative theme.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chewton Mendip Church of England Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
To enrich our music curriculum, all pupils are invited to take part in singing at fetes and celebrations. We hold Chewton's Got Talent every year, where the children can show a wide variety of skills, including piano, violin pieces and songs. Within the school, there have been choirs and a recorder ensemble offered at lunchtime, a Singing for Fun club is beginning in the Summer 2 term. Every Friday Year 4 has strings lessons, and then small group and individual lessons are also offered with Charlotte Sloane-Hill. Throughout the year we hold music assemblies for our string instrument students and pianists to showcase their work to families and their peers.
Our Year 4 pupils were delighted to perform in a special whole-school music assembly alongside children from across the school who receive weekly individual piano and string lessons. Parents of the performers were also invited to join us, making it a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the children's musical achievements and growing confidence as performers.
For our Year 4 pupils, the performance showcased the musical knowledge and skills they have developed throughout the year in line with the Key Stage 2 National Curriculum. Through learning to sing and play with increasing accuracy, fluency, control and expression, the children demonstrated their understanding of rhythm, pitch and dynamics, performing as part of an ensemble while listening carefully to one another. They also developed their ability to appreciate and evaluate music through regular opportunities to rehearse, refine and perform.
For those receiving weekly individual piano or string tuition, the assembly was a chance to celebrate the progress they have made through their dedication and practice. Performing to an audience helped to develop their confidence, resilience and musicianship, while giving them the opportunity to share their talents with friends, family and the wider school community.
A heartfelt thank you goes to Charlotte for organising this wonderful event and for her dedication in teaching and encouraging the children throughout the year. As always, the performance was a proud reflection of the commitment, perseverance and enthusiasm shown by every pupil involved, and a fitting celebration of the musical journey they have enjoyed this year.
We benefited from visits by a local choir, Village Voices, and in March 2026 we took part in an Opera, The Team Mascot, based on The Daughter of the Regiment by Donizetti, which was arranged through Jackdaws Music Education Trust.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chewton Mendip Church of England Primary School - Science
pageCache.text:
Science
May 2026 - Gardening
Our Year 2 pupils planted vegetables that had been donated by one of our parents. This supported their Science learning about plants and growing, helping them to understand what plants need to survive and how food is grown. The children enjoyed getting hands-on in the garden and are excited about watching their vegetables grow.
May 2026 - Noah's Ark class trip
Our Reception and Year 1 class visited Noah's Ark Zoo Farm in Bristol. We took part in an animal senses workshop, exploring the different ways animals use their senses to navigate our world. The children had the opportunity to see, touch, smell and listen to a variety of animals in both the workshop and around the zoo site. We had a tractor ride to see the elephants and some of the agricultural fields surrounding the zoo farm. We learnt interesting facts as we walked around the enclosures and used a map to guide us. Some of our favourite animals we saw during the day included the capybara, tigers, snakes, the weaver birds and gibbons. It was a fabulous day!
April 2026 - Animal visits
Linking to their Science learning, Robin class has some very cute visitors! They have been learning about animals and how to look after them. We were grateful that two of our families brought in their bunnies and ducklings for us to see, stroke and ask questions about. We learnt about how to look after them, where they live and what they look like when they are fully grown rabbits and ducks.
To enrich our Science curriculum, we hosted a special ‘Growing Together’ afternoon, inviting parents to join their children in a shared celebration of science learning across the school. Each classroom offered exciting opportunities to explore a different scientific theme through hands-on investigation.
In Robin Class, children explored the science of rainbows, discovering creative ways to make them using light, reflection, water, movement and food dye. The hall was transformed into a space-themed hub, where families worked together on challenges such as choosing suitable materials to repair space gloves and safely landing a Lego spaceship using pushing and pulling forces.
In Woodpecker Class, children tested how far different paper aeroplane designs would fly, while Buzzard Class focused on the human body, measuring, investigating and thinking carefully about how our bodies work.
It was wonderful to welcome so many families, and we are incredibly grateful for their support in making the afternoon such an engaging and memorable celebration of science.

Safeguarding statement
At Chewton Mendip CofE VA primary school; Safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children is everyone’s responsibility. Everyone who encounters children, their families, and carers, has a role to play.
To fulfil this responsibility effectively, all professionals will make sure their approach is child centred. This means we always consider what is in the best interests of the child.
We take an ‘it can happen here’ approach where safeguarding is concerned. Everyone who encounters children has a role to play in identifying concerns, sharing information, and taking prompt action.
We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children by:
There may be occasions when we must consult with other agencies before we contact parents, particularly in relation to child protection concerns. If this is necessary, we will ensure we speak to parents about the concerns raised at an appropriate time. We work closely with Somerset Safeguarding Children Partnership. A link to their website can be found below.
If you would like more information about our procedures, please speak to one of our Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs)

Curriculum
Curriculum at Chewton Mendip Primary School
“The seed fell into good ground and grew up increasing and yielding thirty, sixty and a hundred times as much” Mark 4:8
We are “Growing Together” to become the best we can be and enjoy “life in all its fullness.” (John 10:10)
We are like the seeds growing in the good soil in the Parable of the Sower. We grow and learn together every day. Our school is the good soil where we are cared for, encouraged and helped to flourish.
Our values of Kindness, Respect, Perseverance, Responsibility, Honesty and Courage are the strong roots and enable us to try our best and become confident, caring people, following the teachings of Jesus.
Staff, pupils, families and the local community work together as a team to provide a safe, nurturing and inclusive environment for everyone to reach their full potential and achieve our school aims.
At Chewton Mendip Primary school we committed to ensuring children receive a broad and balanced curriculum that motivates them to develop their understanding of the world around them. We aim to deliver a curriculum that engages children in learning, develops curiosity and makes links across subject areas. Children are given opportunities to apply what they have learnt in a range of contexts through activities and enrichment events that excite and motivate them to want to learn more.
Our learning environment extends beyond the school grounds to the local woods and surrounding village. We ensure that the children are well supervised, though still allowing them the freedom to play and interact with their environment.
All children participate in regular ‘forest school’ sessions. These are led by our qualified staff and enable pupils to problem solve and work as a team.
We embrace all elements of a healthy lifestyle, developing healthy minds and healthy bodies. We ensure that all children engage in at least two hours of physical activity a week and have access to extended school opportunities to maintain their physical fitness. The benefits of outdoor activities are recognised.
Information on how we support children with SEND to access the curriculum can be found in our SEND policy and information report. SEND Policy
We are a small school with four mixed age group classes. To ensure children cover all the statutory curriculum requirements, we work on a 2-year curriculum cycle. We use the KAPOW schemes of work for Science, History, Geography, DT and PSHE.
Each curriculum area has been carefully mapped out to ensure there is a clear progression in knowledge and skills as children move through the school, and that they cover all the national curriculum objectives.
Detailed information on the curriculum can be found here:
We are currently working on Cycle B 2026/2027
We follow the ‘Little Wandles Letters and Sounds Revised’ to teach phonics in Reception and Key stage 1 to teach children to read. Children can be taught past Key stage 1 if they need this support. Children are taught phonics daily where they are taught Grapheme-phoneme correspondence. (GPC) This is the process of matching both the grapheme (the symbol) and phonemes (unit of sound) together and vice versa. The programme is organised so children are taught more simple GPCs first and then complex ones, taking into account the frequency they occur in the most commonly encountered words.
Graphemes are taught and practised in words, sentences and later in fully decodable books. Books sent home are carefully matched to learning that has taken place in school and the graphemes taught. Children review and revise tricky words and GPCs daily. Children who are not keeping up with their peers are identified quickly and given additional support.
At the end of Year 1 children are assessed using the national phonics screening check. This identifies where children may need additional support to enable them to become confident and fluent readers.
Parents can find videos to support the teaching of phonics and reading, and information on the Little Wandles programme using this link:
For parents - Letters and Sounds (littlewandlelettersandsounds.org.uk)
At Chewton Mendip Primary School we use the 'Little Wandle' reading scheme for KS1 pupils. Books are read in school, in line with the children's home reading scheme and their phonic learning.
Our reading scheme in KS2 ensures children are taught all reading skills to enable them to become confident and fluent readers. Texts are carefully selected to ensure children have exposure to a range of different text types.
Information on the progression in reading and an outline of the texts we will be using can be found here:

pageCache.pageTitle: Chewton Mendip Church of England Primary School - Lunchtime clubs
pageCache.text:
Lunchtime clubs
We aim to provide a wide range of opportunities during lunchtimes, giving children the chance to explore their interests, develop new skills and enjoy time with friends.
Below is our timetable of lunchtime clubs and activities for the current term. Children are encouraged to get involved and try something new, and we always welcome their ideas and suggestions for new clubs and activities later in the school year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chewton Mendip Church of England Primary School - School Clubs
pageCache.text:
School Clubs
All children are invited and encouraged to continue "Growing Together" and enjoy “life in all its fullness” (John 10:10), by attending our extra-curricular clubs.
After-school clubs are available to book on Scopay for the following sessions:
Monday - 3.30-4.30pm
Hockey Club - all ages
Run by Matt Cairns Children's Sports Coaching - EVOLVE Sports Coaching
Wednesday - 3.30-4.30pm
Autumn and Spring term - Football - KS2
Summer Term - Athletics - KS2
Run by Matt Crowcher
Thursday 3.30 - 4.30pm
Art Club - Years 1-6
Run by Sally Wetherall
We also run a range of extra-curricular clubs at lunchtimes, including Lego club, Environment club, Singing and Football.
In the summer term, we also run a swimming club.
We want all our children to enjoy “life in all its fullness” (John 10:10), so please contact us with any concerns around your child accessing any of our clubs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chewton Mendip Church of England Primary School - SEND
pageCache.text:
SEND
Chewton Mendip Primary school is an inclusive school where we are “Growing Together” to become the best we can be and enjoy “life in all its fullness.” (John 10:10)
Our staff plan learning and use resources to meet the learning needs of the pupils in their class. We use a range of approaches which support children with additional needs and offer a range of interventions and programmes.
Mrs S. Dalwood is our Special Educational Needs & Disability Co-ordinator (SENDCo). She can be contacted via the school office.
Information on our approach can be found here:
Somerset Local Offer
Somerset’s SEND Local Offer is a hub of information, advice and guidance about the support and services available locally to children and young people aged 0-25 years with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) and their families.
This can be accessed here: Somerset’s SEND Local Offer
